newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S POSTABANK LENDS $170MLN TO HTCC.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S POSTABANK LENDS $170MLN TO HTCC.

text.p: Hungarian Telephone and Cable Company (HTCC) said it replaced a previously planned private placement of bonds in the U.S. with a $170 million credit ten-year credit facility from Hungary's Postabank Rt.
"The loan from the bank is both more flexible and on better terms than the dollar-denominated bond issue," HTCC senior vice-president Andrew Nicholson told Reuters.
The interest of the loan is 2.5 percent over the average of Hungary's six- and twelve-month Treasury bill yields, he said.
Nicholson added that Hungary's Treasury bill yields have showed a declining trend and the forint-denomited loan from Postabank is a good tool for handling devaluation risks.
The proceeds of the credit facility will be used to repay debts and finance HTCC's expansion in Hungary, the company said in a statement.
HTCC is the largest local telephone concession operator in Hungary.
The company plans to use some $94 billion of the facility for repaying earlier credits, including a $75 million, one-year bridging loan granted by Citibank in April, Nicholson said.
From the rest of the funds HTCC will finance the construction of telephone networks in its five local concessions in Hungary, he added.
